english.title: Insider dealer encouraging dealing in securities
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having information as an insider, encouraged **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to deal in securities that were price-affected securities in relation to that information, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the dealing would take place by

(A)_[the acquisition of securities on a regulated market]_
(B)_[the disposal of securities on a regulated market]_
(C)_[the said **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) relying on a professional intermediary]_
(D)_[the said **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) acting as a professional intermediary]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 52(2)(a) and 61(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 1993.

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Secretary of State or the Director of Public Prosecutions is required before proceedings may commence.
(ii) SI 2021/1173 amended the penalty for this offence as of 1st November 2021. For an offence committed before that date use this offence wording. For an offence committed on or after that date, see H23074.
(iii) Where an offence is found to be committed over a period of two or more days, or at some point during a period of two or more days, it is to be taken to have been committed on the first of those days, see section 31(4) of the Financial Services Act 2021.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or the statutory maximum fine.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
